patterns_found.visual_evidence: Both sketches show a narrow top utility/header bar separated from the rest of the page by a long horizontal rule and positioned as a persistent top strip above the main content.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Header/utility navigation should likely remain fixed or sticky while scrolling so the top links and logo remain accessible across the long profile content.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch does not explicitly show scrolling states, so the bar could also be static; stickiness is inferred from the persistent top-bar treatment and common responsive behavior.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: Below the large image area, both sketches show grouped text blocks arranged like multiple content sections under a single profile area; combined with the reference HTML for a profile page, this strongly implies switchable secondary information sections rather than all content being simultaneously expanded.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: A tabbed interface would switch between profile subsections such as biography, publications, or related info without leaving the page. Active tab state and associated panel visibility need JS.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The hand sketch does not explicitly draw tab labels, so this could alternatively be static columns of content; the inference is strengthened mainly by the profile-page context.

sketch_notes: The sketches imply a fairly low-JS profile/detail page rather than an application-style interface. Across both mobile and desktop, the main likely behaviors are a persistent top navigation/header treatment and switchable profile subcontent panels. No clear evidence appears for hamburger navigation, dropdowns, forms, modals, accordions, or progressive loading in the sketches themselves; the desktop version mainly changes layout density, while the underlying interaction model appears consistent across viewports.
